$comment: Model aliases by intelligence tier, plus the permission reviewer's chain. Aliases cannot target other aliases, so every entry is a concrete model. Rung order is ADR-0103's: the lead is the strongest model that answers in that tier, then turn completion observed in this harness, then agentic benchmark evidence, then the cheaper model. Prices, monthly caps and index scores are deliberately absent — they move between syncs, so `/sync-models` reads them from `bin/pi-model-cost` instead of trusting prose here (ADR-0118). Every opencode-go rung spends one shared quota at its own price, and each model's monthly cap only decides how much of that pool it may draw, so a paid Go rung behind another fires only on a failure specific to the first and outlives it only on a larger cap: a tier carries the best paid Go model, then at most one whose cap is strictly larger, and no more, because the rest are never reached (ADR-0122; mid's rungs 4-7 had zero attempts in the retained logs). A tier still spans claude-bridge, opencode-go and the free opencode-go models because those are separate pools, which is the only availability hedge a rung list can hold; the free models close `cheap` and `mid` after every scored rung (ADR-0120) and here longcat-2.5-free and hy4-flash-free have one reviewer prompt each as their only evidence, while beam-free takes no images and stays reviewer-only. `top` alone may head with a rung above the 25% single-prompt drain the script flags, because that tier answers rarely and glm-5.3's cap keeps it answering after the head locks out; the head is gemini-4-argon for that reason and is not repeated in `cheap` or `mid`, whose turns are frequent. `reviewer` is ordered for latency and availability rather than capability: Gemini's free tier and the free Go models still answer in 1–2s once the paid quotas are gone, while Haiku averages ~10s of session startup, so firstEventMs stays 30s to cover Haiku's tail and gemini-3.5-flash-lite's 28s. claude-bridge serves the reviewer only through the pi-claude-bridge#216 standalone-prompt patches and refuses a follow-up review's multi-turn conversation either way, hence followUpReviews off. Groq stays out: its free tiers cap at 2–8k TPM against a ~14k-token reviewer prompt. muse-spark-1.3-contributor is the strongest cheap Go model on the board and is unusable: the endpoint answers 400 until the account opts into endpoints that train on request data.
